TYF should capture real author-session hiccups and agent misreads as local, review-only tooling learning candidates so Alexander can write two books while surfacing practical improvements to TYF. Learn from SOLO's local-only fbs learn pattern, but keep TYF independent of SOLO and avoid storing manuscript source text or snippets.

Build the first local TYF book workbench slice: a file-backed Draft Review Workbench where the author can view/edit candidate draft beside the approved manuscript, see book typeface/paragraph style and image asset scaffolding, and prepare selections for the controlled Gate without uncontrolled manuscript writes. Defer print-ready KDP/PDF, full pagination, publisher templates, and full WYSIWYG layout to later work.

TYF's author-facing workbench should evolve beyond a single prompt/chat and a single candidate draft file into a double-surface local authoring cockpit: a full contextual amanuensis chat plus a free editable draft/manuscript work surface. The author should be able to select arbitrary text, ask the amanuensis about that selection, attach author notes to lines/segments, promote notes into footnotes, work across multiple draft/manuscript units, and use a full-book graph to understand cross-chapter/phrase implications of changes. The experience should preserve TYF's hidden apparatus and Gate discipline while reducing the limitations of a non-interactive single text input.

TYF should support a Codex-aware local workbench architecture where the amanuensis can remain available as a Codex skill while a local web UI stays two-way aware of the same book state. The preferred design is a local TYF daemon/event bus that watches the workspace and serves the browser UI; Codex lifecycle hooks publish session/prompt/tool/turn events into that bus; a TYF MCP server exposes current workbench state, selection, notes, book graph, and safe actions to Codex; and, when full in-browser amanuensis chat is desired, the workbench can use Codex app-server or SDK to start/resume/steer a Codex thread and stream agent events. The integration must preserve plain-file source of truth and Gate discipline.

TYF changed intent and latest-main recovery intake, 2026-06-27. Release vector: TYF is a truthful local amanuensis for an author starting or continuing a real book now, not a cybersecurity prison and not a developer-first protocol. The beta should be judged by time-to-writing, time-to-return-to-writing, and whether the author can preserve source/voice, work in drafts, and consciously move accepted prose through the Gate. Workbench target: TYF should provide a local double-surface Workbench alongside the Codex/Cowork amanuensis. The author needs a full free-text contextual chat plus a physical writing surface where they can edit draft units, select text, ask the amanuensis about the selection, attach author notes to lines/segments/images/book-level targets, convert suitable notes into footnote candidates, see a read-only approved manuscript preview, and prepare Gate packets without direct manuscript writes. Book body shape: draft and manuscript are multi-file surfaces. The Workbench and MCP bridge should treat chapters/sections/threshold pages/images as units, not assume one long Markdown file. Existing formatted or illustrated material and arbitrary dumped chats/folders/zips need arrival containment plus LLM-assisted organization/analysis before writing. Transparency: the author should not need to manually call TYF skills or generate context packets. Hooks/reflexes should be TYF-identifiable, calm, non-irritating, and should read active context automatically. Questions should be substantive gentle attention, not generic doubt in the author's judgment. Amanuensis boundary: TYF itself must not mention SOLO, Alexander-specific harnesses, or private PAI machinery in author-facing work. SOLO is governance for this repo, not TYF doctrine. TYF may borrow patterns, never private identity or runtime lore. Typographer-redactor: full-work body treatment is core for existing manuscripts. The typographer is real redactor craft in the Milchin/editorial tradition: typography, rubrication, structure, language treatment, AI-cadence cleanup, register preservation, image/layout awareness, and print/PDF readiness direction. It is not merely punctuation or em-dash replacement. Bridge safety: Codex/MCP/Workbench hooks may write draft/review/status/note artifacts but must not write manuscript text. Manuscript writes remain proposal -> audit -> author review packet -> author decision -> tyf write --decision. Latest-main check findings to recover as correction pressure: GitHub main is green on hosted 3.9/3.12 CI, but local Python 3.13 found collection failure from importlib-loaded dataclass module not being inserted into sys.modules before exec, an MCP tool failure where first_text is called with a default argument it does not accept, and architecture contract/RC doctor false positives because the marker scanner flags its own forbidden marker definitions and prose strings rather than actual forbidden routes or writes. README/release evidence should not overclaim test counts without matching the current suite and local support matrix.

R1. Local-first single-book amanuensis beta Source: PR #1, `codex/solo-tyf-improvements`, merged 2026-06-27T00:48:13Z. TYF should be a local-first single-book amanuensis beta with a clear author entry, controlled Gate, Codex skill/plugin surface, automatic author reflex hooks, portability documentation, and release hygiene. It should preserve author sovereignty while making the author able to start and return to real book work.

R2. Typographer-redactor is core for existing manuscript bodies Source: PR #1. TYF should include a `typographer-redactor` lane and `tyf treat` review-only treatment surface for substantial existing manuscript bodies. This is redactor craft, voice, typography, and language treatment, not merely punctuation cleanup or more philosophical interviewing.

R3. Workbench target state is a local double-surface writing desk Source: PR #1, `docs/WORKBENCH_TARGET_STATE.md`. TYF should evolve toward a local double-surface Workbench: multi-unit draft/manuscript body, contextual amanuensis chat, selection-aware author notes, note-to-footnote flow, Codex/MCP awareness, safe concurrency, and a derived book graph. Manuscript writes remain behind the Gate.

R4. First runnable Workbench slice supports actual writing, not only chat Source: PR #3, `workbench-v06-local-double-surface`, merged 2026-06-27T03:50:13Z. TYF should provide a runnable local Workbench with book-map sidebar, multi-unit draft discovery, read-only manuscript preview, editable draft surface with compare-and-swap saves, draft unit creation, author notes, footnote-candidate packets, Gate packets, active context packets, loopback server token protection, MCP tools, Codex hook recorder, Codex bridge scaffold, and no manuscript write API.

R5. Workbench integration should expose TYF-named safe tools, not raw filesystem power Source: PR #3. The Workbench MCP bridge should expose TYF concepts such as active selection, unit context, author notes, graph search, footnote candidates, Gate packets, status, and conflicts. It should not expose raw arbitrary write-file tools or direct manuscript writing.

R6. Live Workbench status should make the desk visibly alive Source: PR #5, `workbench-next-slice-status-conflicts-approvals`, merged 2026-06-27T04:08:40Z. TYF should show live Workbench status for Codex activity, draft state, stale-draft detection, and approval requests. The status model should be read-only, local, and loopback by default.

R7. Workbench author language should be calm and action-oriented Source: PR #6, `workbench-realtime-status-sse`, merged 2026-06-27T08:12:07Z. TYF should make the browser surface calmer and clearer with labels such as Assistant status, Save safety, Needs your approval, Safe to save, Changed outside this window, Prepare for manuscript review, Share this moment, and Make footnote candidate. Product calm matters more than more machinery.

R8. Realtime Workbench updates should be read-only and local-first Source: PR #6. TYF should provide a read-only realtime Workbench update path through server-sent events with polling fallback. The endpoint must not create a manuscript write route, and draft writes should continue using compare-and-swap helpers.

R9. Book graph is a rebuildable projection, not a new source of truth Source: PR #7, `workbench-graph-projection-ledger-audit`, merged 2026-06-27T08:59:12Z. TYF should derive a provenance-first book graph from existing local truth files. Graph JSON and optional SQLite cache are rebuildable artifacts. Deleting them must not delete author knowledge.

R10. JSONL files require explicit storage semantics Source: PR #7. TYF should distinguish hash-chain ledgers, mutable JSONL record stores, append logs, empty placeholders, and broken ledgers. A `.jsonl` extension alone is not a ledger.

TYF should provide a non-rewriting polish review that reads local voice-map and typography-style records, reports narration-lane mismatch, register leaks, dash style drift, ellipsis style drift, and key-term capitalization drift, and points to exact lines without rewriting sections or manuscript files.

These contracts should be machine-readable and checked by tests or doctor tooling.
